rule: Negative subject focus uses the embedded/subjunctive negative aan fused with baa/ayaa rather than ordinary main-clause ma.
source: John I. Saeed, Somali (1999), Simple Sentences focus discussion; Heine & Reh (1984), Grammaticalization and Reanalysis in African Languages; John I. Saeed, The Functions of Focus in Somali
note: Unaccented baan is orthographically ambiguous with baa + 1sg aan in other constructions. The project therefore requires exact reviewed predicate/context evidence before assigning the negative-subject-focus reading.

rule: When negation co-occurs with focus, Somali uses a reduced subjunctive. In the simple aspect the reduced negative form does not distinguish present from past and does not distinguish person/number.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar (University of Gothenburg, Aug. 2023), p. 94, Reduced subjunctive forms
source_principle: Reduced subjunctive forms are used with negation plus focus; simple heesin serves both past and present and is person/number neutral.
project_execution: Reuse only exact project morphology already reviewed as person-neutral negative simple forms (for example cunin, iman/imanin, aqoon). In negative focus, reinterpret them contextually as reduced_subjunctive_simple with temporal scope present_or_past. No suffix derivation.

rule: When negation co-occurs with focus, progressive reduced subjunctive forms likewise do not distinguish present from past or person/number.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar (University of Gothenburg, Aug. 2023), p. 94, Reduced subjunctive forms
source_principle: Reduced progressive heesayn(in) is listed for both past and present subjunctive under negation plus focus.
project_execution: Reuse only exact project morphology already reviewed as person-neutral negative past-progressive surfaces (for example cunayn/cunaynin and imanayn/imanaynin). In negative focus, reinterpret them contextually as reduced_subjunctive_progressive with temporal scope present_or_past. No unseen form is generated.

rule: A common-noun subject focused by negative baan/ayaan remains in the absolute/non-subject case, as in affirmative baa/ayaa subject focus. The negative reading is assigned only when predicate/context evidence independently supports negation.
source: Heine & Reh subject-focus case rule plus Saeed negative-focus rule
note: Do not globally reinterpret baan/ayaan as negative because they can overlap subject-clitic spellings in non-subject focus.

rule: Negative focus habitual uses an exact reviewed habitual stem followed by person-neutral reduced auxiliary jirin.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar (University of Gothenburg, Aug. 2023), p. 94; Qaamuuska Af-Soomaaliga CUN/IMOW paradigms for exact stems and negative jirin
project_execution: Execute only when both pieces are independently reviewed: a stem licensed for habitual-with-jir (currently exact forms such as cuni and imaan) plus exact negative auxiliary jirin. Do not derive new stems or allow arbitrary verbs before jirin.

rule: In ordinary spelling, baan may represent negative subject focus (baa + negative aan) or non-subject focus with a first-singular subject clitic (baa + 1sg aan). Saeed shows otherwise identical written strings whose spoken pitch distinguishes the readings.
source_examples: Faarax baan qaban — Faarax did not catch him
Faarax baan qaban — I will catch Faarax
source: John I. Saeed, Somali (1999), pp. 193–194, examples 36–39
project_execution: If a predicate surface itself has a reviewed non-negative verb analysis as well as a covered negative analysis, written baan/ayaan is not enough to choose negative subject focus. Keep the clause unjudged unless exact sentence evidence or independently reviewed negative-context evidence disambiguates it.

rule: waxba is a negative constituent/polarity expression meaning roughly nothing/not anything and can independently support a negative clause reading.
source: John I. Saeed, Somali (1999), negative declaratives discussion; Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar, particle -ba discussion
project_execution: waxba may strengthen a negative reading but never determines subject/object role by itself. It is used only after structural focus checks succeed, especially when the predicate surface also has a reviewed non-negative analysis.

rule: True negative subject focus requires negative aan to be fused with baa/ayaa. Bare baa/ayaa is not equivalent to baan/ayaan before an independently reviewed reduced negative predicate.
source: Saeed negative-focus rule; Gothenburg negative-question contrast Ma Cali baa tegay / Ma Cali baan tegin
project_execution: When a reviewed focused subject is followed by bare baa/ayaa and a covered reduced negative predicate, report a marker conflict with expected baan/ayaan. Keep autofix off because interpretation still requires review.

rule: Negative focus future uses an exact reviewed future stem followed by person-neutral reduced auxiliary doonin.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar (University of Gothenburg, Aug. 2023), p. 94; Qaamuuska Af-Soomaaliga CUN/IMOW paradigms for exact future stems
project_execution: Execute only when the stem is independently reviewed for future-with-auxiliary use (currently exact forms such as cuni and imaan) and the auxiliary is exact source-backed doonin. Keep ordinary ma-future doono/doonto/doonno/doontaan/doonaan separate.
